chains.title: Alt G preserves an AP-2α (TFAP2A) site in the IRF6 enhancer MCS9.7; ref A disrupts it, lowering IRF6 in oral periderm/keratinocytes
chains.element: MCS9.7 / IRF6 enhancer ~10 kb upstream of IRF6 (chr1q32.2)

links.claim: The G (alt) allele matches the AP-2 consensus (GCCNNNGGC-like) and is bound by TFAP2A, while the A (ref, risk) allele weakens or abolishes that binding; TFAP2A is chosen within the AP-2 specificity group because it is the family member mutated in branchio-oculo-facial syndrome with orofacial clefting and is expressed in surface ectoderm.
The variant lies in the conserved MCS9.7 enhancer, which drives reporter expression in oral periderm, medial edge epithelium and other IRF6 domains.
Reduced TFAP2A occupancy lowers enhancer output and hence IRF6 transcription in cis.
IRF6 dosage is critical in the periderm/keratinocytes of the fusing lip and palate shelves.
Partial IRF6 loss impairs periderm differentiation and epithelial fusion, raising risk of non-syndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate.

predictions: Allele-specific TFAP2A ChIP (or ChIP-qPCR) in keratinocytes shows preferential occupancy on the G allele
TFAP2A knockdown reduces MCS9.7 reporter activity for the G construct much more than for the A construct
MCS9.7-A reporter gives lower activity than MCS9.7-G in oral keratinocytes
IRF6 allelic expression imbalance in heterozygous lip/palate epithelium favouring the G chromosome
falsified_if: EMSA/ChIP shows equal or A-favouring occupancy by AP-2 proteins
TFAP2A knockdown leaves allelic reporter difference unchanged
No allelic difference in MCS9.7 enhancer activity in relevant epithelial cells

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant itself: risk is carried by a linked variant in the IRF6 locus
predictions: No allelic difference in MCS9.7 reporter activity or TF occupancy
Fine-mapping/conditional analysis points to another variant in the same haplotype block
Base-editing the single position in keratinocytes leaves IRF6 expression unchanged
falsified_if: Reproducible allele-specific enhancer activity or TF binding at this exact position
Isogenic single-base edit changes IRF6 expression

chains.title: Same enhancer and direction, but the AP-2 family member acting at the site is TFAP2C

links.claim: The AP-2 motif affected is bound in surface ectoderm mainly by TFAP2C, which shares the AP-2 binding specificity; alt G binds more strongly than ref A. TFAP2C is chosen because it is highly expressed in embryonic basal keratinocytes and periderm and can be the dominant family member there.
MCS9.7 contains the AP-2 site and functions as an epithelial enhancer.
Loss of TFAP2C binding on the A allele reduces IRF6 enhancer activity.
TFAP2C is the predominant AP-2 paralog in periderm at the stage of lip fusion.
Reduced IRF6 in periderm predisposes to cleft lip.

predictions: TFAP2C, not TFAP2A, knockdown abolishes the allelic reporter difference
TFAP2C ChIP shows stronger signal than TFAP2A at MCS9.7 in keratinocytes
Supershift of the G-allele EMSA complex by anti-TFAP2C but not anti-TFAP2A antibody
falsified_if: TFAP2C is not expressed or not bound at MCS9.7 in relevant cells
Allelic effect persists unchanged after TFAP2C depletion

chains.title: The variant alters a p63 (TP63)-dependent regulatory module rather than an AP-2 site
chains.element: MCS9.7 IRF6 enhancer, adjacent p63 response element
chains.cell_type: basal keratinocytes of the oral epithelium

links.claim: The alt G allele supports stronger occupancy of a p63 (TP63, ΔNp63 isoform) half-site or cooperative complex at MCS9.7; the A allele weakens it.
MCS9.7 carries a functional p63 response element and p63 is a known direct activator of IRF6 through this enhancer.
Weaker p63-dependent activation on the A allele lowers IRF6 expression.
ΔNp63 is the master regulator of embryonic oral basal keratinocytes.
The p63–IRF6 regulatory loop is disrupted in orofacial clefting syndromes, so reduced IRF6 raises cleft lip risk.

predictions: Allele-specific p63 ChIP shows G-allele preference at the variant
TP63 knockdown removes the allelic reporter difference while AP-2 knockdown does not
Mutating the AP-2 core alone does not abolish allelic difference
falsified_if: p63 binding at MCS9.7 is allele-independent
The variant lies outside any p63 motif footprint

matrix.test: Luciferase reporter of MCS9.7 with A vs G allele in oral/epidermal keratinocytes

outcomes.outcome: G construct clearly more active than A
G construct clearly more active than A
G construct more active, effect lost in TP63-null cells

matrix.test: EMSA with keratinocyte nuclear extract plus anti-TFAP2A and anti-TFAP2C supershift

outcomes.outcome: No AP-2 supershift; distinct larger complex

matrix.test: Allele-specific ChIP-qPCR for TFAP2A, TFAP2C and TP63 in heterozygous keratinocytes
Isogenic base editing A<->G at the endogenous locus, then IRF6 qPCR

next_experiment: Transient luciferase assay of the MCS9.7 enhancer carrying A versus G in oral keratinocytes: a reproducible allelic difference in enhancer output supports H1 (and H2/H3), while no difference supports the null H4, at minimal cost.
